title: 1996 AHSME Problem 12
statement: A function \(f\) from the integers to the integers is defined as follows: \[ f(n)= \begin{cases} n+3 & \text{if \(n\) is odd},\\ \frac{n}{2} & \text{if \(n\) is even}. \end{cases} \] Suppose \(k\) is odd and \(f(f(f(k)))=27.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(k?\)

solutions.text: Since \(k\) is odd, \(f(k)=k+3\) is even, so \(f(f(k))=\frac{k+3}{2}.\) If this value were odd, adding \(3\) could not produce \(27\) because that would require the value \(24.\) Therefore it is even and is halved to \(27,\) so \(\frac{k+3}{2}=54.\) Hence \(k=105,\) whose digits sum to \(6.\) The correct answer is B.
hints: Because \(k\) is odd, the first iterate is \(k+3\), which is even
Work backward from \(27\), checking the parity required by each inverse branch
